newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property stocks rise after tumble.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property stocks rise after tumble.

text.p: Singapore property shares received an early boost on Wednesday from Wall Street's surge and the government's denial of plans to hold a news conference this week to announce new curbs on the market.
Rumours had been rife of a government announcement of fresh curbs on the housing sector due to be made at the weekend and the property index fell to a six-month low of 639.81 on Tuesday.
However, the Ministry of National Development told Reuters later on Tuesday it had no plans to hold such a news conference and the index started to recover.
By 0130 GMT on Wednesday, the property index had firmed 10.37 points, or 1.6 percent, to 657.33, led by a rebound in heavyweights like Wing Tai and City Developments (CityDev).
CityDev led the gainers, rising Singapore 40 cents to S$11.90 on 715,000 shares while Wing Tai rose four cents to S$3.76 in active volume of over 1.4 million shares.
"The property market has factored in possible new measures. We just don't know when. The point is the knife is already in the heart and it's just a matter of twisting it," a local broker said.
Dealers said the property market was also getting a boost from Wall Street's firmer close.
The Dow surged 179 points to end at 6,962.03 on Tuesday after the release of a weaker than expected wage inflation figure and manufactured goods orders along with a strong corporate earnings report.
The economic data soothed earlier concerns of rising interest rates.
